monitoredModules.name: Az.Resources
monitoredModules.purpose: Observed #193 collision source for Microsoft.Extensions.* transitive assemblies.

evidence: The 2026-10-17 upstream inventory for Microsoft.Graph.Authentication 2.41.2, ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.1, Az.Storage 9.7.2, Az.Accounts 5.5.3, MicrosoftTeams 8.0.0, and Az.Resources 10.2.1 added Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions to the conflict surface and moved Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions to versions 2.2.0.0 and 10.0.0.0; Az.Accounts is now an additional contributor to both paired Microsoft.Extensions assemblies.

Both Microsoft.Extensions assemblies remain classified block under #193: they are incidental transitives and are directly referenced with ExcludeAssets=runtime, so the new upstream copies remain outside DLLPickle's preload bundle. No preload classification changed.

The conflict-surface fingerprint was recomputed to 97cb4339be699089ba06b9be4af6384058a8abd80740290f92c68ed3d901baec, and the refreshed baseline is exercised by the policy-realization guard and the dependency-policy unit and non-live integration suites.

observations: Microsoft.Identity.Client ownership varied by import order, including a private AzSharedAssemblyLoadContext load.
System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData 10.0.0.0 was supplied by the PowerShell host in the Default context.
The preloaded MSAL and IdentityModel assemblies loaded once in the Default context at the resolved DLLPickle versions.
Azure.Core 1.57.0.0 remained in AzSharedAssemblyLoadContext rather than being preloaded.
System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData 10.0.0.0 remained host-provided in the Default context and was not bundled.

runtimeDifferential.verdict: Both configured import orders completed successfully with and without DLLPickle; the differential supports retaining the current preload/block classifications for this update.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: Azure.Core is intentionally not preloaded on any supported modern runtime profile (net8.0, net9.0, or net10.0). Az.Accounts 5.x isolates its Azure SDK stack in a private AssemblyLoadContext; preloading Azure.Core into the default load context splits Azure.Core.TokenRequestContext across load contexts and breaks Connect-AzAccount with a MissingMethodException on InteractiveBrowserCredential.AuthenticateAsync. Graph, Exchange, and Teams resolve a compatible Azure.Core themselves, so the preload is unnecessary for them. The original net48-only Azure.Core preload (#183) does not apply to the modern profiles.

evidence.basis: Runtime probe 2026-05-31: Az.Accounts and Microsoft.Graph.Authentication both self-isolate Azure.Core in private ALCs and run different versions side-by-side (1.50 vs 1.51.1). Preloading into the default ALC splits TokenRequestContext -> Connect-AzAccount MissingMethodException. Removed from the bundle in 2.0.1.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: Azure SDK stack self-isolated by Az.Accounts (and Graph); not preloaded on the supported net8.0, net9.0, or net10.0 profiles.

evidence.basis: Runtime probe 2026-05-31: loaded into Az's private ALC (1.13.0). Belongs to the Azure SDK stack that breaks when preloaded (Azure.Core class). Not bundled by DLLPickle.

evidence.basis: In the conflict surface; part of the Az-self-isolated Azure SDK stack. Not bundled by DLLPickle.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: Azure SDK transitive (Azure.Core dependency) self-managed by Graph/Az; not preloaded on the supported net8.0, net9.0, or net10.0 profiles.

evidence.basis: Runtime probe 2026-05-31: loaded into Graph's private ALC (1.9.0) alongside Azure.Core. Transitive of the blocked Azure.Core. Not bundled by DLLPickle.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: #193: incidental transitive of Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens, not part of DLLPickle's identity-coordination purpose and not host-provided. Excluded from the bundle (ExcludeAssets=runtime) so it does not collide with modules that bundle their own copy (Az.Resources).

evidence.basis: Diagnostic 2026-05-31: DLLPickle preloaded 8.0.0 into the default ALC; PowerShell ships only Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool (not this); Az.Resources 9.x bundles its own copy -> 'assembly with same name is already loaded' on Import-Module Az.Resources. Fixed in 2.0.2.
evidence.trackingScope: Az.Resources is included in monitoredModules so upstream inventory captures this assembly family from the observed #193 collision source. #193 remains a DLLPickle-bundle-vs-consumer collision (not a cross-module version split), so the cross-module conflict-surface gate still may not flag every change by itself; preserve the regression guard against re-bundling in tests/Integration/DLLPickle.IntegrationTest.Tests.ps1 and re-adjudicate runtime behavior when Az.Resources dependency content changes.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: #193: paired with DependencyInjection.Abstractions (depends on it); same incidental-transitive collision with Az modules. Excluded from the bundle (ExcludeAssets=runtime).

evidence.basis: Excluded alongside DependencyInjection.Abstractions in 2.0.2. Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens still loads without it bundled (resolves lazily / supplied by the consuming service modules). The 2026-10-17 inventory confirms the same paired exclusion remains necessary as Az.Accounts now contributes version 10.0.0.0.
evidence.trackingScope: The refreshed inventory now observes Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions from Az.Accounts and MicrosoftTeams at versions 10.0.0.0 and 2.2.0.0. It remains excluded from the bundle as the paired dependency of Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions, which Az.Resources and Az.Accounts ship. #193 remains a DLLPickle-bundle-vs-consumer collision; preserve the regression guard against re-bundling in tests/Integration/DLLPickle.IntegrationTest.Tests.ps1 and re-adjudicate runtime behavior when upstream dependency content changes.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: Logging.Abstractions 10.x introduces DiagnosticSource 10.x even when the logging runtime asset is excluded. PowerShell provides DiagnosticSource for the identity stack; bundling the 10.x assembly causes preload failures on the supported .NET 8 and .NET 9 hosts.

evidence.basis: PR #301 runs 39182858353 and 39182858388 reproduced failures when DiagnosticSource 10.x was bundled on PowerShell 7.4 and 7.5. Run 39236885938 captures the host-selected DiagnosticSource 8.0.0.0, 9.0.0.0, and 10.0.0.0 in the Default ALC across all nine exact runtime/platform profiles; the 10.x package runtime asset remains excluded. After removing DiagnosticSource rows and derived fingerprints, all nine normalized snapshots exactly match the previously accepted evidence.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: Runtime-provided BCL assembly supplied by PowerShell on Windows, so Import-DPLibrary must not preload the bundled copy there. PowerShell does not provide it on Linux or macOS, so the single platform-neutral release artifact must include it for the MSAL extensions dependency chain.

evidence.basis: Windows validation on 2026-06-23 established that PowerShell supplies this assembly. The release pipeline publishes one module artifact assembled on Windows, so excluding the runtime asset at build time also removed it for Linux and macOS. The universal artifact now retains the file, while the shipped runtime profile policy filters it from Windows preloading and permits it on non-Windows hosts.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: Issue #174 showed that default OData preloading can break Az.Storage when ExchangeOnlineManagement and Az.Storage require incompatible OData identities.

evidence.basis: Az.Storage 9.6.1 ships Microsoft.OData.Core 7.6.4; ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.9.2 requires 7.22.0. Both load into the default ALC; no preload version can satisfy both. See issue #174 and the shipped conflict-data entry '174-odata-azstorage-exo' (src/DLLPickle/KnownConflicts.json) for the runtime adjudication.

blockedPreloadAssemblies.reason: Keep the OData family out of the default preload set unless a future isolation strategy is implemented.

evidence.basis: OData family dependency paired with Microsoft.OData.Core; same default-ALC conflict as Core. See issue #174 and the shipped conflict-data entry '174-odata-azstorage-exo' (src/DLLPickle/KnownConflicts.json) for the runtime adjudication.
